inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text: Bloomberg’s own framing gives the game away: as energy prices rise, flights are canceled, and death and destruction dominate the screens, people worldwide are asking when the Iran war will stop. Yet Israel is presented as the exception, with strong public backing to see it through. That contrast is doing useful work: it makes an ongoing war sound like public resolve rather than a choice being sustained by powerful interests. The account doesn’t even finish the thought after “until,” but the omission only sharpens the question of who benefits from keeping this going.
